findings.title: Unbounded per-group queues remove backpressure and can exhaust memory
findings.body: FixedQueuePool creates `queue.Queue()` without a maxsize, so each per-group queue is unbounded, and FixedQueuePool.submit uses a non-blocking `put`. A single slow subscription will keep all of its messages accumulating in that worker's queue while the main Arroyo loop continues polling and submitting. Contrary to the class docstring's 'Natural backpressure when queues fill up', there is no backpressure; memory and OffsetTracker's all_offsets/outstanding sets grow without bound, risking OOM and a stalled consumer. Bound the queue or use blocking put with a timeout, and expose pressure metrics/backpressure.

findings.title: Worker failure still marks offsets complete and commits them
findings.body: In OrderedQueueWorker.run, exceptions from result_processor are caught and logged, then the finally block at line 149 unconditionally calls complete_offset. The commit loop later commits completed offsets, so a failed result is treated as processed and will not be retried or sent to DLQ. This violates the strategy's stated guarantee 'Only commits offsets after successful processing' and can silently drop results when result_processor raises. Complete offsets only in the success path; failures should leave the offset outstanding or be explicitly routed to a retry/DLQ path.

findings.title: Shutdown flag can leave queued work unprocessed
findings.body: OrderedQueueWorker.run checks `while not self.shutdown` at the top of the loop. FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets `worker.shutdown = True` before draining queues. If a worker finishes an item and returns to the top while its queue still has items, it exits without calling get() again, so queued WorkItems and their offsets are never processed by this pool. This contradicts the graceful drain implied by `q.shutdown(immediate=False)` and can cause in-flight backlog to be dropped until the consumer is restarted. The shutdown flag should not be set before queue drain, or the worker should drain until queue.ShutDown before exiting.

findings.title: Negative max_workers creates an empty queue pool that crashes on submit
findings.body: `num_queues=max_workers or 20` passes negative values through (e.g. `--max-workers=-1`). FixedQueuePool.__init__ then `range(-1)` creates no queues/workers, and the first `submit` does `self.queues[hash(group_key) % -1]`, which indexes 0 and raises IndexError. Validate `max_workers > 0` or normalize non-positive values.
